We should clear spec.conditionalAuthorization if the feature is disabled.

If conditional authorization is disabled, clients running a SAR and indicating they would *accept* conditional results should be run unconditionally and only get back unconditional results. We intentionally made it safe to run unconditional authorization in response to an accepting-of-conditional-responses authorization request.

(same comment applies to all the *SAR registry impls)
I prefer this behavior to silently dropping given the consequences of authorization, but @liggitt definitely had opinions.

This just controls the validation layer. If a SAR makes it to validation when the gate is off and has this field set, validation **should** reject it, so that's fine.

However, I **also** think we should clear the field before handing the SAR off to validation if the feature is disabled.

A client asking to do a SAR and indicating it would accept conditional responses is better off if we run unconditional authorization than having their request rejected. No authorizer should unconditionally allow a request it would have only have conditionally allowed.

Initially, I added the `AuthorizationOptions`/`ConditionalDecision` fields consistently to internal, v1 and v1beta1, like is the standard way to do it for APIs that are serialized and need to be able to roundtrip successfully through any external version. However, @liggitt mentioned last week that he'd rather make it impossible to make a `v1beta1` object with conditional fields set. Thus, I removed the fields from `v1beta1`. 

However, if there would be a caller that would like to convert an internal object with e.g. `{Allow, Deny, NoOpinion, ConditionsMap, Union}` to v1beta1, there is no shape of that that keeps the same semantics. Thus I felt it's best to error if anyone tried to do that. So it's not validation per se, but more a question of preserving semantics.

The roundtrip tests are thus adjusted to always set the new fields to `nil`, this always roundtrips.
